projects.title: SeaSure
projects.description: Boat owners describe a problem with text or photos, and SeaSure’s answer takes that boat’s equipment and service records into account. Repairs that need a professional go out as a service request.
projects.detail: SeaSure organizes vessel knowledge around a boat’s systems, installed equipment, manuals, service history, and current issues. Its AI assistance connects that context to troubleshooting and maintenance workflows, helping owners understand a problem and carry useful diagnostic information into professional service.

caseStudy.roleContext: Lihon’s role on SeaSure was AI & Backend Engineer. The overview below describes the product as a whole.
caseStudy.challenge: Boat troubleshooting depends on the specific vessel, installed equipment, documentation, and service history. The product challenge is to keep that information connected as an owner describes an issue and seeks maintenance or professional help.
caseStudy.engineeringContext: The public product materials describe vessel-aware assistance, multiple input formats, persistent records, and service handoffs. The diagram maps how those parts relate.
caseStudy.evidenceSummary: The official website and app listing describe the features covered on this page.

architecture.alt: Conceptual SeaSure flow: vessel context and owner observations inform troubleshooting, with connections to maintenance records and professional service requests.
architecture.caption: Illustrative product flow based on public SeaSure materials. Component boundaries are conceptual, not evidence of deployed architecture.

technicalSections.title: Vessel-aware context and knowledge retrieval
body: A useful marine assistant needs the identity of the boat, its installed equipment, the relevant documentation, and its service history. SeaSure’s product presents these as connected context around the vessel, extending from a system to its manufacturer, model, component, and records.

This gives troubleshooting a specific information boundary: an engine question, an electrical issue, and a navigation problem can be interpreted against different equipment and documentation contexts.

technicalSections.title: Multimodal troubleshooting
body: The public product supports text, photos, documents, audio, video, and live video in its marine assistance experience. The app listing describes specialized AI guidance across engines, electrical systems, hull, navigation, plumbing, and safety.
Whatever the owner sends should stay tied to the same vessel and its documents until the problem is solved.

technicalSections.title: Maintenance records and professional handoff
body: The Captain’s Binder and service-record features organize manuals, registration, surveys, repairs, and maintenance events. When professional assistance is needed, SeaSure carries the boat and diagnostic context into a service request.
This connects conversational assistance to persistent operational records and a real service workflow, rather than leaving the result as an isolated answer.

technicalSections.title: From question to service request
body: The owner’s troubleshooting conversation and the boat’s records sit in the same product. A marine professional who takes the job gets that context with the request, so the owner should not need to explain the problem twice.

projects.title: Dr. Infinity
projects.description: A documented clinical AI design combining medical evidence retrieval, source-linked responses, and local de-identification.
projects.detail: Dr. Infinity approaches clinical AI through evidence retrieval, medical knowledge representation, and information governance. The supplied technical architecture separates local de-identification, hybrid retrieval, domain-adapted inference, and output verification to produce structured, source-linked clinical knowledge responses.
projects.stack: Concurrent vector and medical knowledge-graph retrieval; MeSH and SNOMED CT relationships; domain-adapted LLM synthesis; local in-memory de-identification
projects.visualAlt: Dr. Infinity medical knowledge graph and evidence retrieval concept illustration

caseStudy.roleContext: Lihon’s listed role is AI & Backend Engineer. The technical discussion follows a supplied project brief; individual deliverables and ownership boundaries are not documented here.
caseStudy.challenge: Clinical knowledge questions need relevant evidence, traceable citations, and careful handling of sensitive inputs. The documented design addresses how retrieval, synthesis, and verification can work together while limiting unnecessary exposure of patient information.
caseStudy.engineeringContext: The supplied brief separates local de-identification, concurrent vector and medical-graph retrieval, domain-adapted synthesis, and verification. The diagram summarizes that documented design. It does not establish clinical validation, measured latency, privacy compliance, or deployment behavior.
caseStudy.evidenceSummary: The architecture is described in the project technical brief supplied by Lihon in October 2026. The brief is listed below but is not published here. The project website is available separately; no benchmark report, clinical validation, or individual contribution record is included.

architecture.alt: Documented Dr. Infinity design: local de-identification precedes concurrent vector and medical knowledge-graph retrieval, followed by synthesis and verification of source-linked findings.
architecture.caption: Illustrative diagram of the supplied technical brief. This is documented design, not proof of production behavior or clinical validation.

technicalSections.title: Hybrid retrieval and medical knowledge graphs
body: The technical brief describes concurrent retrieval from a vector index and a structured medical knowledge graph. Semantic similarity retrieves relevant passages, while MeSH and SNOMED CT relationships connect clinical entities and support graph traversal across medical concepts.

Combining these retrieval paths allows evidence selection to consider both the language of a question and the relationships between concepts. Retrieved context can then be cross-referenced before it reaches the language-model synthesis stage.

technicalSections.title: Efficient retrieval-augmented generation
body: Retrieval and generation are decoupled in the documented architecture. Vector and graph lookups run concurrently, reducing the amount of retrieval work that must happen sequentially before evidence can be assembled for inference.

The documented retrieval design targets sub-50 ms index responses. Parallel retrieval, focused context selection, and a staged evidence-to-synthesis pipeline establish the latency budget and the boundaries between indexing, evidence assembly, and generation.

technicalSections.title: Domain-adapted synthesis and multi-agent reasoning
body: The project documentation describes domain-adapted language models working with medical literature and cross-referenced findings. PubMed, FDA labels, and peer-reviewed journals are identified as evidence sources, with medical fine-tuning and multi-agent reasoning included in the design.

The synthesis stage turns retrieved material into structured findings while preserving the relationship to supporting evidence. This treats retrieval quality, clinical vocabulary, and response structure as explicit system concerns.

technicalSections.title: Evidence grounding, provenance, and verification
body: Line-item citations, source provenance, automated source indexing, and audit metadata make generated statements traceable to retrieved literature. A verification layer is described as checking assertions against supporting material before the final response is assembled.

These mechanisms support inspectable clinical knowledge workflows: the response, its source context, and the evidence path can be reviewed together. Grounding and audit metadata make retrieval decisions visible throughout the synthesis pipeline.

technicalSections.title: Privacy-aware ingestion and deployment boundaries
body: The supplied design describes local, in-memory de-identification of the 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier categories before outbound transmission. It also specifies AES-256-protected payloads, avoidance of raw EHR storage, and a zero-retention architecture.

Private-cloud and on-premise deployment options address institutional control over clinical information and EHR data sovereignty. These deployment boundaries complement local de-identification, encrypted payloads, and retention controls in the documented privacy architecture.

technicalSections.title: Expected practical benefit
body: Combining retrieved medical passages with knowledge-graph relationships is intended to make supporting evidence easier to inspect. Local de-identification is intended to limit unnecessary identifier exposure before outbound processing. These are design goals; clinical accuracy, privacy behavior, and performance have not been independently validated here.

projects.title: WanduBot
projects.description: WanduBot’s private search runs on SearXNG and lets users pick the upstream engines and privacy settings. A separate chat interface, WanduGPT, is part of the same product.
projects.detail: WanduBot brings privacy-focused web search and a dedicated WanduGPT chat experience into one product ecosystem. Its SearXNG-backed metasearch interface makes retrieval configurable across general web results and specialist information sources, while exposing practical controls for search privacy, languages, and upstream engines.
projects.stack: SearXNG-based metasearch; configurable upstream search engines; a dedicated WanduGPT conversational interface
projects.visualAlt: WanduBot private search and conversational AI concept illustration

technicalSections.title: Privacy-first search architecture
body: WanduBot positions its public search service around untracked searching and states that it does not collect or store search data. The product emphasizes user control over search behavior rather than a persistent search-preference profile on the server.

Privacy is also visible in the interface: settings expose query submission, image proxying, tracker-parameter removal, and whether a search query appears in the page title. These are configurable protections, allowing users to choose how much query context is exposed through browser history, page metadata, and external resources.

technicalSections.title: Federated retrieval and search orchestration
body: The search interface identifies SearXNG as its underlying metasearch technology. A configurable set of upstream search engines gives users access to multiple information sources through a common query interface.

General web search sits alongside images, video, news, maps, music, IT, science, files, and social categories. Engine selection, displayed weights and time limits, and visible response and reliability information make source selection an explicit part of the retrieval experience.

technicalSections.title: Configurable query and result privacy
body: The preferences interface offers GET or POST query submission, an optional image proxy, and tracker URL cleanup. POST submission can keep the query out of the address bar; proxying image requests can reduce direct resource requests to image hosts; tracker cleanup removes configured tracking parameters from result links.

These controls serve different data-exposure boundaries and remain user-selectable. Browser-stored preference cookies preserve settings for convenience, according to the preferences page; that configuration storage is distinct from a behavioral tracking profile.

technicalSections.title: Language-aware retrieval and relevance controls
body: Language detection, multilingual search preferences, SafeSearch, autocomplete configuration, and category selection let users adapt retrieval to their research context. A technical question, a scientific reference search, and an image lookup can use different categories and source preferences.
Queries are handled the same way whichever engines a user picks, and each privacy option is easy to understand.

technicalSections.title: Conversational AI alongside search
body: WanduGPT supplies a separate public conversational AI interface alongside the search product. Together, the two surfaces cover source discovery and open-ended AI interaction.

Search configuration and conversational interaction form distinct product surfaces. The project brings source discovery, query controls, and open-ended AI interaction together around privacy-oriented information access.

technicalSections.title: Limits of the privacy settings
body: With these settings, users decide which upstream engines receive a search and how much of the query shows up in browser history and page titles. That gives control over some kinds of exposure, but it is not anonymity.
